reconcile.note: Clarke distinguishes two senses of 'tempt': Deuteronomy's testing versus James's denial that God can be enticed to sin.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses that the command not to tempt God would be pointless unless God actually could be tempted, contrary to James's flat denial.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.
sides.verseText: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.

sides.snippet: Let no man say when he is tempted, \"I am tempted by God,\" for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
sides.verseText: Let no man say when he is tempted, \"I am tempted by God,\" for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
